# Separate AI review of the v5 norm refinement

Date: 22 October 2026.

The local derivation in [the note](v5-norm-refinement.md) is supported under its stated hypotheses. The derivative majorant with coefficient $26$ follows on $1<s<51/50$, $v\ge22$, for fixed shifts independent of $s$. The two printed error thresholds also have elementary proofs. The quotient application retains its other rounded enclosure premises.

This statement records a separate OpenAI Codex agent review. The authoring and reviewing agents belong to the same model family. The reviewer reconstructed the argument before comparing the completed note and used a different elementary route for the thresholds. This is not independent human peer review, a proof assistant result, or an independently executed arithmetic certificate.

The review checked the whole line summation hypotheses, the two second derivatives, the logarithm signs, the factor $w^{-3}$, and the coefficient $26=15+11$. It also checked local uniform convergence for differentiation in $s$, the uniform endpoint bound at $v=22$, the quotient signs and positive denominator, and the distinction between the actual error and a difference of upper bounds. The source attribution and fixed corrected v5 version were retained.

An alternative threshold route uses

$$
\pi<\frac72,\qquad \zeta(3)<\frac54,\qquad
-\zeta'(3)<\frac14,\qquad \log22<\frac{16}5.
$$

For the first bound, integrate $1/(1+x^2)<1-x^2+x^4$ on $0<x<1$ to obtain $\pi<52/15<7/2$. The decreasing integral tail gives $\zeta(3)<1+1/8+\int_2^\infty x^{-3}dx=5/4$.

On $1<x<2$, the inequalities $1/2<1/x<(3-x)/2$ give $1/2<\log2<3/4$. Thus $(\log x)/x^3$ decreases for $x\ge2$, and its strict integral tail gives

$$
-\zeta'(3)<\frac{\log2}{4}+\frac1{16}<\frac14.
$$

The differentiated Dirichlet series is justified by the same local summable domination stated in the note. Positivity of the exponential series gives $e>8/3$ and $e^{1/5}>6/5$, hence

$$
e^{16/5}>\left(\frac83\right)^3\frac65
=\frac{1024}{45}>22.
$$

These bounds give, by hand,

$$
E(22)<\frac{385}{2044416}<\frac1{5000},
\qquad
n_{41}(22)<\frac{4053}{2044416}<\frac1{500}.
$$

The cross products are $385\cdot5000=1925000<2044416$ and $4053\cdot500=2026500<2044416$. The note's different route to the same thresholds was also checked, including its positive integral identity for $\pi$, exponential truncation and final rational comparisons.

No mathematical software, full numerical verifier or proof assistant was run for this review. The remaining enclosures for $\zeta(2\sigma)$, $c_\sigma$, $\kappa$, the main term and the endpoint are not certified here. Neither novelty, a new discriminant cutoff, nor the complete underlying theorem is claimed.

Acceptance by hand: recover $26=15+11$, verify either complete threshold route, and check $2(A_0+F)(U-U_{26})=d$ while retaining the stated remaining assumptions.

# An elementary refinement of the v5 norm error bound

Date: 22 October 2026.

The derivative error estimate in twinheterodox's v5 argument admits a smaller elementary majorant: the bracket constant can be reduced from $41$ to $26$, with the same domain and normalization. This note also proves the two printed error thresholds by exact hand inequalities and explains how the improvement propagates through the norm quotient.

The baseline is [twinheterodox, `tenth-discriminant`, corrected v5, norm series estimate](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/6f781492afd06de32997c2c89d4e228a78bab7fc/versions/v5/proof.tex#L522-L574). Its arithmetic application belongs to the inherited branch $2000\le q\le4000$. It does not address the later numerical band near $570$, establish a new cutoff, or settle the complete argument. The analytic lemma below needs no class number hypothesis.

## Statement and assumptions

Let $v\ge22$, $1<s<51/50$, and let $\tau_b\in\mathbb R$ be fixed shifts, independent of $s$. Define

$$
A_v(s)=\sum_{b\ge1}\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}
\bigl((a+\tau_b)^2+(vb)^2\bigr)^{-s},\qquad
F_v(s)=C(s)v^{1-2s}\zeta(2s-1),
$$

$$
C(s)=\int_{\mathbb R}(1+y^2)^{-s}\,dy.
$$

The source uses $\tau_b=b/2$. All derivatives with respect to $s$ in this note keep $v$ and the shifts fixed. Put

$$
E(v)=\frac{11\pi\zeta(3)}{24v^3},\qquad
n_k(v)=\frac{\pi}{24v^3}
\left[(k+22\log v)\zeta(3)+22(-\zeta'(3))\right].
$$

We prove

$$
|A_v(s)-F_v(s)|\le E(v)\le E(22),\qquad
|-A_v'(s)+F_v'(s)|\le n_{26}(v)\le n_{26}(22).
$$

The source's derivative majorant is $n_{41}(22)$. The exact saving between the two uniform majorants is

$$
d:=n_{41}(22)-n_{26}(22)
=\frac{15\pi\zeta(3)}{24\cdot22^3}>0.
$$

This compares upper bounds, not the actual error. No value of $d$ or final endpoint margin is evaluated here.

## Convergence and the summation estimate

For a sufficient version of whole line Euler summation, let $h\in C^2(\mathbb R)$, assume $h,h''$ are absolutely integrable, $h,h'\to0$ at both infinities, and assume the shifted sum converges absolutely. With $\widetilde B_2$ the periodic extension of $B_2(t)=t^2-t+1/6$, two integrations by parts on each unit interval, followed by telescoping, give

$$
\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}h(a+\tau)-\int_{\mathbb R}h(x)\,dx
=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\widetilde B_2(x-\tau)h''(x)\,dx.
$$

The boundary hypotheses justify passage to the whole line. Since $\sup|\widetilde B_2|=1/6$, the absolute error is at most $\frac1{12}\int|h''|$. This is also the whole line specialization of [NIST DLMF, Euler Maclaurin formula 2.10.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/2.10.E1): its constant Bernoulli contribution integrates to $h'(+\infty)-h'(-\infty)=0$.

The actual functions are $f_s(x)=(x^2+w^2)^{-s}$ and $g_s(x)=\log(x^2+w^2)(x^2+w^2)^{-s}$, where $w=vb\ge22$. They and their first spatial derivatives vanish at infinity; the functions and their second derivatives are integrable, and their shifted sums converge absolutely. Powers of $|x|$, with at most one logarithm, give these bounds directly.

Parameter differentiation needs local uniform convergence. On a compact interval $[s_0,s_1]\subset(1,51/50)$, choose $1<r<s_0$ and set $\epsilon=s_0-r$. For $Q\ge1$,

$$
Q^{-s}\le Q^{-r},\qquad (\log Q)Q^{-s}\le\epsilon^{-1}Q^{-r}.
$$

Monotonicity on each half line bounds every shifted row, uniformly in its shift, by

$$
\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}((a+\tau)^2+w^2)^{-r}
\le2w^{-2r}+C(r)w^{1-2r}.
$$

Both terms are summable over $w=vb$, $b\ge1$, because $r>1$. The corresponding integrals have the same domination. Thus the series and integrals may be differentiated termwise near every allowed $s$. Scaling the horizontal integrals gives $F_v(s)$, and the logarithm weighted sums and integrals equal $-A_v'(s)$ and $-F_v'(s)$, respectively. No assertion at $s=1$ is needed.

## Where 41 becomes 26

Write $Q=x^2+w^2$ and $L=\log Q\ge0$. Direct differentiation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_s''&=-2sQ^{-s-1}+4s(s+1)x^2Q^{-s-2},\\
g_s''&=2Q^{-s-1}(1-sL)
+4x^2Q^{-s-2}\bigl(s(s+1)L-(2s+1)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

Using $0\le x^2/Q\le1$ and $L\ge0$,

$$
|f_s''|\le(4s^2+6s)Q^{-s-1}<11Q^{-s-1},\qquad
|g_s''|\le\bigl(6+8s+(4s^2+6s)L\bigr)Q^{-s-1}
\le(15+11L)Q^{-s-1}.
$$

The coefficient bounds follow on $1<s<51/50$. The source instead uses the valid but looser coefficient $19$ in place of $15$.

After $x=wy$, the common scale factor obeys

$$
w^{-2s-1}(1+y^2)^{-s-1}\le w^{-3}(1+y^2)^{-2}.
$$

All factors multiplying it are nonnegative. The substitution $y=\tan\theta$ gives $\int_{\mathbb R}(1+y^2)^{-2}dy=\pi/2$. For the logarithmic integral, use

$$
J:=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\log(1+y^2)}{(1+y^2)^2}\,dy
\le\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{y^2}{(1+y^2)^2}\,dy
=\pi-\frac\pi2=\frac\pi2.
$$

The source uses $J\le\pi$, obtained from $\log(1+y^2)\le1+y^2$. Its coefficients therefore give $19+22=41$. The two refinements give $15+11=26$, while $\log(w^2)=2\log w$ leaves the coefficient of $\log w$ equal to $22$.

Euler summation applied separately to $f_s$ and $g_s$ now bounds their row errors by

$$
\frac{11\pi}{24w^3},\qquad
\frac{\pi}{24w^3}(26+22\log w),
$$

respectively. Summing over $b$ yields $E(v)$ and $n_{26}(v)$, since $\sum b^{-3}=\zeta(3)$ and $\sum(\log b)b^{-3}=-\zeta'(3)$. This derives the derivative error from $g_s$, rather than differentiating an error inequality.

For $k=26$ or $41$,

$$
\frac{d}{dv}\bigl(v^{-3}(k+22\log v)\bigr)
=v^{-4}(22-3k-66\log v)<0\quad(v\ge22).
$$

The other term of $n_k(v)$ is a positive constant times $v^{-3}$. This proves the uniform endpoint bounds and the stated exact saving $d$.

## Two error thresholds proved by hand

The following coarse bounds suffice:

$$
\pi<\frac{22}{7},\qquad \zeta(3)<\frac54,\qquad
0<-\zeta'(3)<\frac5{16},\qquad \log22<\frac72.
$$

For the first, polynomial division and $\int_0^1(1+x^2)^{-1}dx=\pi/4$ give

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&<\int_0^1\frac{x^4(1-x)^4}{1+x^2}\,dx\\
&=\int_0^1\left(x^6-4x^5+5x^4-4x^2+4-\frac4{1+x^2}\right)dx
=\frac{22}{7}-\pi.
\end{aligned}
$$

The decreasing function $x^{-3}$ gives $\zeta(3)<1+1/8+\int_2^\infty x^{-3}dx=5/4$. Also $1/2<\log2<1$, by integrating $1/x$ on $[1,2]$, so $(\log x)/x^3$ decreases for $x\ge2$. Thus

$$
-\zeta'(3)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\log n}{n^3}
<\frac{\log2}{8}+\int_2^\infty\frac{\log x}{x^3}\,dx
=\frac{\log2}{4}+\frac1{16}<\frac5{16}.
$$

The derivative series identity follows from uniform convergence near $3$: on $5/2\le s\le7/2$, the bound $\log n\le2\sqrt n$ dominates its differentiated terms by $2n^{-2}$.

Finally, the exponential Taylor remainder after degree four is positive at $7/2$, so

$$
e^{7/2}>1+\frac72+\frac{49}{8}+\frac{343}{48}+\frac{2401}{384}
=\frac{3075}{128}>\frac{2816}{128}=22.
$$

This proves the logarithm bound without a numerical approximation. Substitution in the two positive majorants gives

$$
E(22)<\frac{11(22/7)(5/4)}{24\cdot22^3}
=\frac{55}{325248}<\frac1{5000},
\qquad 55\cdot5000=275000<325248,
$$

$$
n_{41}(22)
<\frac{(22/7)\bigl[(41+22\cdot7/2)(5/4)+22\cdot5/16\bigr]}{24\cdot22^3}
=\frac{1235}{650496}<\frac1{500},
\qquad1235\cdot500=617500<650496.
$$

These establish the printed allowances $E_A=0.0002$ and $E_N=0.002$. They also prove $0<d<n_{41}(22)<E_N$ and $n_{26}(22)<E_N-d$. These hand comparisons use no software evaluation of special functions, verifier execution, or other mathematical software.

## Conditional propagation to the arithmetic quotient

For this application, assume a prime $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $2000\le q\le4000$, and class number one for $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-q})$. Set $v=\sqrt q/2>22$, $\sigma=71/70$, and $\tau_b=b/2$. The units are $\pm1$. Counting ideal generators up to these units and using the ideal Euler factors gives the [source's primitive norm identity](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/6f781492afd06de32997c2c89d4e228a78bab7fc/versions/v5/proof.tex#L471-L520)

$$
B_q(s)=\frac{\zeta(2s)+A_v(s)}{\zeta(2s)}
=\prod_{p\,\mathrm{split}}\frac{1+p^{-s}}{1-p^{-s}}\,(1+q^{-s}).
$$

The differentiated product converges locally uniformly for $s>1$, dominated on compact subintervals by a constant times $\sum_{n\ge2}(\log n)n^{-s_0}$, $s_0>1$. Write $D(s)=\sum_{p\,\mathrm{split\ or\ ramified}}(\log p)p^{-s}$. Positivity of the split higher powers yields

$$
D(s)\le-\frac{B_q'(s)}{2B_q(s)}+\frac{\log q}{q^s},\qquad
-\frac{B_q'}{B_q}=\frac{N-cA}{z+A}\ge0,
$$

where $A=A_v(s)$, $N=-A_v'(s)$, $z=\zeta(2s)>1$, and $c=-2\zeta'(2s)/\zeta(2s)>0$. The sign of $N-cA$ follows from the Euler product, not merely from $N,A\ge0$.

Evaluate at $s=\sigma$, put $F=F_v(\sigma)>0$, $N_F=-F_v'(\sigma)$, $\ell=\log(q/4)$, and define

$$
\kappa=-\frac{C'(\sigma)}{C(\sigma)}
-\frac{2\zeta'(2\sigma-1)}{\zeta(2\sigma-1)}-c.
\qquad N_F-cF=F(\ell+\kappa).
$$

For fixed $N\ge0$ and $z,c>0$, the quotient decreases with $A$ on $A>-z$; it increases with $N$ when the other variables are fixed. Since $z+F-E_A>1-E_A>0$, the proved error allowances give

$$
\frac{N-cA}{z+A}
\le\frac{F(\ell+\kappa)+E_N+cE_A}{z+F-E_A}.
$$

This does not require $F-E_A\ge0$. It follows either by differentiation or by cross multiplication: with $N_+=N_F+E_N\ge N\ge0$ and $A_-=F-E_A$, the numerator difference is $(N_+-N)(z+A)+(A-A_-)(N+cz)\ge0$.

Retain the source's remaining rounded premises as assumptions:

$$
z>1.61893624,\qquad c<1.090928,\qquad65<\kappa<69.106001.
$$

They are not proved by this note. Exact rounding gives $E_N+1.090928E_A=0.0022181856<0.002219$ and $1.61893624-E_A=1.61873624$. The upper bound on $c$ is used only in the positive term $cE_A$, after applying the exact cancellation identity. Replacing $c$ directly in $N-cA$ would have the wrong direction.

With $A_0=1.61873624$, the [printed template](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/6f781492afd06de32997c2c89d4e228a78bab7fc/versions/v5/proof.tex#L576-L609) is

$$
D(\sigma)\le U(q):=
\frac{F(q)(\ell+69.106001)+0.002219}{2(A_0+F(q))}
+\frac{\log q}{q^\sigma}.
$$

Since $n_{26}(v)\le n_{26}(22)<E_N-d$, the same argument retains a uniform symbolic improvement:

$$
D(\sigma)\le U_{26}(q):=U(q)-\frac{d}{2(A_0+F(q))}<U(q).
$$

The new numerator stays positive because $d<E_N<0.002219$. Uniformity comes from the decreasing refined majorant $n_{26}(v)$; it does not assert that $n_{41}(v)-n_{26}(v)\ge d$ for $v>22$. Rounding both budgets back to $E_N$ would discard the improvement.

For the smooth comparison templates, $x=\log q$ gives $F_x=-\rho F$, where $\rho=\sigma-1/2=18/35>0$. Hence

$$
\frac{d}{dx}\frac{d}{2(A_0+F)}
=\frac{d\rho F}{2(A_0+F)^2}>0,\qquad (U_{26})_x<U_x.
$$

Any previous transfer based on a one sided upper bound for $U_x$ is preserved when its other premises are unchanged. This differentiates smooth templates, not a prime sum indexed by discriminants. The remaining enclosures and endpoint comparison are still needed for an arithmetic conclusion.

## Attribution, limits, and acceptance

See the [separate AI review](v5-norm-refinement-review.md) and [source provenance](v5-norm-refinement.provenance.json) for the review scope and source identities.

The source credit belongs to twinheterodox's v5 construction. The pinned file is `versions/v5/proof.tex` at commit `6f781492afd06de32997c2c89d4e228a78bab7fc`, with SHA256 `d080fd1cbdea6e6426ff173124dd7be7c9984ad7ec2230cb9f9d5eb539d8f74f`. This note gives a local refinement and its explicit hypotheses; it makes no claim of priority or global novelty.

OpenAI Codex assisted the derivation and drafting. Separate agents from the same model family reconstructed the local arguments before comparison. That is AI review, not human peer review. No Lean or other proof assistant checked these results, and no full source verifier was run for this note.

Acceptance by hand: recover the coefficient $26=15+11$, check local uniform convergence, multiply out the positive integral identity for $\pi$, and verify the integer comparisons $275000<325248$ and $617500<650496$. For the conditional application, check

$$
2(A_0+F)(U-U_{26})=d
$$

while keeping the three remaining rounded premises and the endpoint comparison separate. These checks establish the stated local bounds without claiming a new cutoff or a complete proof of the underlying number theoretic theorem.

# Polymath Make mathematical research easier to check, reproduce, and hand to the next reviewer. Polymath is a Rust CLI that checks a finite mathematical certificate, records bounded verification runs, retrieves research notes, and compares the scope of different claims. It keeps the artifact, its assumptions, and the evidence together.

The included example covers **4,075 candidate integers** from Tao's tenth discriminant challenge. A successful check establishes that every candidate has a valid finite witness. The broader number theory argument remains a separate responsibility. ## Try it You need Rust and Cargo. Clone the repository, then run the commands below from its root. Cargo may download dependencies on the first build; the CLI makes no AI provider calls. ```sh git clone https://github.com/ruvnet/Polymath.git cd Polymath ``` Start with the read only demo: ```sh cargo run --locked --release -- demo ``` Check the example directly: ```sh cargo run --locked --release -- verify examples/tao-32768.certificate.json ``` Record a verification run and inspect its journal: ```sh cargo run --locked --release -- run --id example-001 --certificate examples/tao-32768.certificate.json --state .polymath cargo run --locked --release -- status --state .polymath ``` Find related notes and compare claims: ```sh cargo run --locked --release -- recall examples/research-notes.json --query 'determinant valuation' --limit 3 cargo run --locked --release -- compare examples/claims.json ``` The `run` command creates local state and permits at most four started verifications per journal. Repeating a completed ID with the same certificate, expected bounds, and executable returns the saved receipt. A changed request under that ID is rejected and stops the journal. An interrupted or failed run blocks new work for inspection. The other commands above inspect inputs without starting an optimizer. This local allowance does not reset, resume, or spend any earlier Tao numerical research allowance. To persistently stop a local journal, use `cargo run --locked --release -- stop --state .polymath`; there is no automatic reset command. ## What a passing check means The example examines integers satisfying `163 < q < 32768` and `q ≡ 3 mod 8`. It verifies complete coverage and the arithmetic witnesses in the certificate. The file is 6,486 bytes and contains 4,075 candidates. Three mathematical inputs remain outside that finite check: 1. The analytic argument reduces the problem to `q < 32768`. 2. Any hypothetical remaining fundamental discriminant of class number one lies in the stated residue class. 3. The stated small noninert prime obstruction rules out class number one. | Evidence | What it establishes | | :--- | :--- | | Exact certificate check | Every candidate in the specified finite domain has a valid witness. | | Journal receipt | A particular local action and artifact were recorded with their result. | | Separate mathematical review | A reviewer has examined the general argument and its assumptions. The CLI does not supply that review. | | Formal proof | A proof assistant accepts a precisely encoded theorem and its dependencies. Lean is not implemented here. | A journal receipt, a policy decision, or an admission check does not turn finite evidence into a general theorem. The example explicitly retains `global_proof_verified: false`. ## Research notes The [v5 norm estimate note](docs/research/v5-norm-refinement.md) derives a refinement from 41 to 26 in one derivative error bound and proves the two required error thresholds using elementary rational estimates. It concerns the inherited interval from 2000 to 4000. It establishes no smaller discriminant cutoff. The [review statement](docs/research/v5-norm-refinement-review.md) records separate Codex agent checks, including a second route to the threshold inequalities. This is AI assisted written mathematics, with no human peer review or Lean verification claimed. ## What is connected | Component | Current role | Boundary | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Rust exact verifier | Checks the included finite obstruction certificate. | No analytic cutoff proof or general theorem checker. | | Local journal | Records bounded verification actions and their results. | Local evidence; no independent attestation. | | [rGi](https://github.com/ruvnet/rGi) | `demo` and `run` call the pinned policy evaluator for certificate verification. | A policy kernel, not an autonomous runtime or independent mathematics checker. | | [RuVector](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruvector) | Uses an in memory HNSW index to retrieve research notes. | Approximate lexical similarity from hashed tokens, not semantic embeddings or proof confidence. | | [Autogenous](https://github.com/ruvnet/autogenous) | `demo` and `run` call pinned upstream mutation admission code after exact verification. | Checks declared metadata structure, not certificate contents; no fitness judgement, signed promotion, or rollback execution. | | [Ruflo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo) | Can coordinate the surrounding research project. | No Ruflo agent runtime is embedded in this CLI. | | ruOS | Can provide an existing environment in which to run the CLI. | This repository does not provision or remotely control a host. | | Metaharness | A future adapter for proposing and evaluating bounded experiments. | The earlier search loop has not been ported into this Rust CLI. | There is no autonomous AI provider runtime, automatic mathematical discovery, or paid compute provisioning in this release. The animated diagram describes the research workflow; separate review remains work for a reviewer. ## Use it for a research contribution Start with one claim whose inputs and acceptance condition can be written down. Keep its proposed artifact separate from the checker. Record the source version and assumptions, run the exact check, and give the artifact and receipt to a separate reviewer. Compare claims by their conclusions, assumptions, checked ranges, and review status. A smaller cutoff, a shorter certificate, and a faster verification are different results. The `compare` command helps keep those distinctions visible; it does not rank mathematical truth. The main remaining uncertainty in the example is the general analytic dependency chain. Improving the certificate or its journal does not resolve it. The useful next step is a separate review of one named mathematical obligation. ## Provenance The example grew out of work on [Terence Tao's tenth discriminant challenge](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/10/20/an-experimental-ai-math-challenge-using-tenth-discriminant-bounds-to-explore-arguments-ruling-out-siegel-zeroes/). Its finite domain follows the [elementary companion in twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/tree/a9a5a43655516927e1c74cdb7ce74cef95eda7bf/companions/elementary). The certificate was generated in that research workflow; it is not a new analytic bound. The upstream papers and challenge contributions retain their own authorship and review status. We link to them rather than redistribute their papers. This repository makes no claim to a challenge record, a new theorem, or priority for their mathematical ideas. The [fixture provenance](examples/PROVENANCE.json) records its exact hash, source, and scope; [third party notices](THIRD_PARTY.md) identify the upstream software. # Architecture

Polymath makes a proposed mathematical artifact inspectable through an exact check and a local evidence record. The Rust CLI is the executable boundary. The general mathematical argument, the review of that argument, and any future experiment generator remain separate.

## Data flow

1. A person supplies a certificate, notes, or claims file.
2. The command validates its input. `demo` and `run` also evaluate the tool policy before certificate verification.
3. The certificate verifier checks the finite domain and witnesses using exact arithmetic.
4. A recorded run stores the artifact identity and outcome in the local journal.
5. A reviewer can inspect the result together with its assumptions and source provenance.

The diagram in [research-loop.svg](assets/research-loop.svg) illustrates that workflow. Its animation is presentation only. It does not imply that the CLI generates conjectures, runs AI agents, or performs independent mathematical review.

## Command boundaries

| Command | Input | Output | State effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `demo` | Bundled finite example | Certificate and integration checks | No research run or optimizer is started. |
| `verify` | Certificate JSON and expected domain | Exact verification result | Direct arithmetic check; no policy gate, admission step, or journal run. |
| `run` | Explicit run ID, certificate, state directory | Recorded verification result | Writes local journal state under the stated cap. |
| `status` | State directory | Current journal status | Inspection only. |
| `stop` | State directory | Persistent stopped status | Prevents new recorded verifications. |
| `recall` | Research notes, query, result limit | Related note records | Builds an in memory retrieval index. |
| `compare` | Claims JSON | Comparison of scope and evidence | Inspection only. |

The new local verification allowance is independent of the earlier Tao research workflow. It authorizes no numerical parameter search and changes none of that workflow's counters, caps, accepted artifacts, or automation state.

## Journal behavior

Each journal permits at most four started runs. A request binds the certificate hash, expected bounds, and executable hash to its ID. Repeating a completed request returns its stored receipt. Reusing an ID for a changed request records a conflict and stops the journal, including after an executable change.

The journal reserves a pending entry before dispatching verification. Failures remain recorded. A pending or failed entry blocks new work rather than automatically retrying it under a different identity. A process lock prevents concurrent writers. Completed receipts are compared with their stored journal copies before further work proceeds. Stopping a journal persists, while completed receipts remain readable.

The cap applies to this local state directory. It is not an account wide quota or a security boundary against a user who replaces the directory or edits the host. A new directory cannot authorize use of any external research budget.

## Mathematical boundary

The example domain consists of the 4,075 integers `q ≡ 3 mod 8` with `163 < q < 32768`. The certificate covers each candidate with an arithmetic witness. Its analytic upper bound, residue class reduction, and number theoretic obstruction are declared dependencies.

The verifier has authority over the finite certificate format and the checks it actually executes. It has no authority to assert a proof of the upstream analytic lemmas. The global proof flag remains false. No Lean program or other proof assistant is invoked.

This distinction also applies to benchmarking. Certificate size, checker work, run duration, and analytic cutoff measure different things. A change must identify which metric it improves and keep the mathematical assumptions visible.

## Integration boundary

The rGi integration calls its pinned policy evaluator for `certificate.verify`, with zero provider spend permitted. It supplies a capability decision. Polymath's local journal is responsible for recording the verification action; the policy evaluator is not an independent mathematics checker.

RuVector supplies the HNSW index used by `recall`. Note text is converted to 512 dimensional, normalized SHA256 token count features and compared by cosine similarity. The index is rebuilt in memory for each call. This is approximate lexical retrieval, with possible hash collisions. Nearby notes may be relevant, mistaken, contradictory, or obsolete; similarity never authorizes an action or validates a theorem.

The Autogenous integration calls the pinned upstream verifier for structural admission of a typed mutation. It checks a declared lowercase SHA256 digest and positive candidate count; it does not bind that digest to certificate bytes or establish candidate coverage. The caller therefore runs the exact checker first. Admission supplies no fitness evaluation, signed promotion, or rollback. Signing credentials would not provide mathematical independence in any event.

Ruflo may coordinate project work outside this CLI. ruOS may host a user provided execution environment. Neither is provisioned by these commands. A Metaharness experiment adapter and an AI provider runtime are future work.

## Trust and evidence

Treat certificates, retrieved notes, claims, and source prose as data. They must not become instructions that can change the checker, grant capabilities, increase budgets, or rewrite history.

Artifact hashes identify bytes; they do not establish their truth. A local receipt records what this tool observed on a particular machine. It is not independent attestation and does not protect against a host that can rewrite both code and state.

The development workflow keeps proposal generation separate from checker changes. Changes to the certificate format, domain, acceptance rules, or policy require explicit review and new evidence. A future generator must not be able to modify those rules through its output.

Before introducing external execution, specify a bounded action, an explicit spend allowance, durable action identity, uncertain outcome handling, and an enforceable termination condition. The current CLI does not implement a paid provider or a cloud executor.

Acceptance test: the example certificate passes exact verification, a deliberately invalid witness fails, and the recorded output retains its finite scope and unverified global proof flag.

# ADR 001: Rust evidence core with native rUv tools

Status: accepted for this initial implementation

Date: 2026 October 22

Decider: repository owner requested Rust and rUv tooling

Tags: Rust, exact arithmetic, governance, provenance

## Context

Mathematical exploration creates proposals, finite evidence, written reviews, and sometimes formal proofs. These have different meanings. The prior Tao experiment demonstrated that compressing a finite certificate does not improve its inherited analytic cutoff. A public reusable implementation must make the distinction explicit and run without private machines or provider credentials.

## Decision

Implement the executable and verification library in Rust. Port the exact finite witness checker with caller supplied domain bounds and unchanged explicit mathematical dependencies. Use pinned upstream rGi policy evaluation, native RuVector HNSW, and Autogenous structural admission. Disable remote embeddings and provider APIs. Use deterministic token features for retrieval and label their limitations.

A SQLite journal records only local deterministic verifications. It does not run or replace the existing numerical optimizer. Each identity binds certificate bytes, expected bounds, and the actual executable hash. A process lock serializes writers. Completed identities replay; conflicting, failed, pending, stopped, or exhausted states reject new dispatch. Conflicts are retained and persistently stop the journal. Partial state is never automatically replaced. An immutable receipt must agree with the journal before reuse. Four started recorded verifications per state directory are the local demonstration limit, with no reset command. Standalone verification remains a read only checker.

Claim comparison checks declared metadata only. Different assumptions or bound relations do not receive a numerical ranking. No metadata status, vector similarity score, structural admission, or signature establishes mathematical truth. The code never sets global proof, formal proof, or state of the art flags to true.

## Consequences

A clean clone can reproduce finite evidence and run real rUv libraries locally. Git pins and Cargo.lock bind the software inputs. The known finite fixture covers 4075 candidates in 163 < q < 32768 with q congruent to 3 modulo 8. It does not prove the analytic cutoff or congruence reduction.

Native dependencies increase first build time. Retrieval uses lexical features rather than learned semantic embeddings. Autogenous admission is structural; signed promotion is not implemented. The journal detects ordinary file drift and process interruption, but an administrator who rewrites both state and receipts is outside the threat model. SQLite and filesystems are trusted for persistence. There is no automatic recovery for ambiguous runs.

This repository introduces no new Tao numerical allowance and does not migrate production sources or histories. A future optimizer, Lean verifier, ruOS remote adapter, or metaharness search adapter needs its own explicit design and review.
